Leaning on his staff, he descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he said: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. Having abandoned the deep village, one enters the wild weeds once more.
Even as one passes through layer after layer, one does not know that the encounter grows deeper and the evasion becomes more subtle. Ultimately, how is it? The mind..."
"This is Buddha; wisdom is not the Way.
He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "Of the springtime's ninety days, two-thirds have already passed. Everywhere in the gardens, the red is diminishing and the green increasing.
The orioles migrate to the lofty trees, and the swallows build new nests; they too are busily occupied. As for the gate of the patch-robed monks..."

[The Master] descended from his seat. Furthermore, how is it? Incense burning in the burner, sitting in stillness, doing nothing at all; day after day it is the same, morning after morning it is thus.
[He] struck the meditation bench and said: "If one cannot yet be like this, how can one be like this?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "One clarity clarifies all; one realization realizes all. When the Way is non-existent, it is not not so; when the Way is existent, it has never been existent.
Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind upon this long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous."
Incense Offering on the Anniversary of Wuzu Heshang’s Death: Smiling with a hidden malice so deep, he twists thorny ropes to the left to bind the ghost-child alive;
he holds the tail of a scorpion upside down to bring calamity upon the common folk. Although I stepped across his threshold, fortunately I did not suffer from the stench of his poison.
How can this be seen? Inserting the incense, he says: "This alone serves as proof."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'Open the gate of expedient means; reveal the true reality. [He strikes the floor with his staff once and] says:
'The gate of expedient means has opened. Where is the true reality? [He strikes the floor once more and] says: 'A few wisps of white clouds enshroud the ancient temple;
a single ribbon of green water winds around the verdant mountains.'"

Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the fourth month: In the past, Māyā gave birth to a lump of iron; though it was given the name "Siddhārtha," a name beyond naming, they attempted to cast a golden body from it but could not succeed.
To have cast it at all was a great error—truly an error! To this day it burdens the people of our Eastern Land;
year after year they wash it, yet only produce more dust.
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "The Patriarch said: 'You who study the Buddha-dharma are like planting seeds;
my preaching of the essential Dharma is like the moisture from heaven. By this we know that seeds must exist, yet the moisture of heaven cannot be absent.
However, too much rain harms the crops, and too many words cause one to drift further from the Way. Now, how can one attain resonance?"
"Go! Pulling up seedlings to help them grow is not my business; the clods of earth, the rain, and the breezes will not deceive you.
He ascended the hall and cited the teachings: "This matter can only be known by me," and again, "Only Buddhas and Buddhas can know it," and also, "It is like a person drinking water;
whether it is cold or warm, they know it for themselves. If this is so, then as for the Buddhas appearing in the world and the Patriarchs...

The Master came from the West; it cannot be said that his labor was not in vain. Nevertheless, were it not for Liu Yi’s transmission of the letter, who would have seen the profundity of the Dragon King’s palace?
Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: when one is bound, all are bound; when one is released, all are released.

When both binding and releasing are forgotten, the entire body is carefree and elegant—to the point of being beyond mere elegance. One sheds the cage and net; like a great fish released into the vast abyss, or a single wild goose soaring into the high heavens.
Xie Bingfu ascends the hall. When both meaning and phrasing reach their full expression, one does not enter deep villages nor enter the wild weeds.

When meaning and phrasing do not reach their full expression, the coral forest is bright with the blazing sun. But what of it when a single word exhausts the path, yet the underlying intent remains beyond reach? How is this?
After a long silence, he said: "The land of Wu ends at the river; beyond the bank, the mountains of Yue abound.
When Head Seat Xuan arrived, he ascended the hall and held up his alms bowl at the position of Nanquan. His "Tiger-trapping" device was profound;
he brought Linji before Huangbo out of a sincere concern for others. Such an eye, such an action—throughout past and present.
Without interval; before and after, there is no difference. A solitary wild horse flies high, chasing the setting clouds.

[The Master] ascends the hall and addresses the assembly, saying: "The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials, the Five Ranks of Ruler and Subject, speaking of the partial and the orthodox, distinguishing host and guest—these do not avoid adding further dust to the eyes.
He takes up his staff, makes a stroke in the air, and says: "I cut it all off at once!"
Vast and boundless as space, the solitary wild goose flies far away—where can it be known? Outside the gate, the falling leaves rustle incessantly. On the Mid-Autumn Festival, an old friend arrived;
he ascended the hall and said: "I deeply cherish the Mid-Autumn moon; its many emotions are like those of an old friend.

How bright it shines in the heavens! It illuminates me again and again. Its perfect form follows the flowing stream; its pure radiance is utterly free from a speck of dust. Lofty and solitary, I reach out to it..."
It is not that it is lacking; meeting face-to-face is the closest intimacy.
Entering the hall [the Master said]: "In the midst of late autumn, neither cold nor warm; the wind is fine and the rain is misty. The water is clear and the clouds are thin.
At such a time as this, is there still the meaning of the Patriarch from the West? After a long silence, he said: "A single oar."
Mist and waves; reeds on both banks. The Buddha’s Way: ascending the hall.
Six years on the Snowy Ridge, how many times did the snow fall? It was not just this current bone-chilling cold.
At the third watch of the night, one cannot hold back; for no reason, the Big Dipper looks toward the south. Gautama, Gautama! Open your eyes!
When dawn broke in the heavens, he did not realize the red sun was already three *gān* high.
He ascended the hall, took up his whisk, and called to the assembly, saying: "This single grasp has been passed down by all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past."
Even the elder monks throughout the world are all at their wits' end. Can you all manage it? Do not say that you cannot;
I, this mountain monk, am also at my wits' end. Since we are all at our wits' end, what is the ultimate reality? After a long silence, he said: "When the snow melts, one knows the earth is warm;
when the clouds clear, one sees the sky is high."
Record of the Sayings of the Abbot at Taiping Xingguo Chan Monastery on Mount Yang in Yuanzhou;
Compiled by those who have studied under him.

On the seventeenth day of the fifth month in the first year of the Xianchun era, the Master entered the monastery. Taking his seat in the Abbot’s quarters, he said: "In the past, the Old Vimalakīrti..."
"Ma! Take up your brush and model it; clearly delineate two five-foot lengths, yet insist that they are one *zhang* long.
If you do not believe me, come back in five days when there is nothing else to do and try measuring them yourself."
Provincial Decree. The Way of the Patriarchs is like a person in a thousand-foot well; without the aid of even a foot of rope, how could they get out?

Why do you make it so difficult for yourselves? Today, the Grand Councilor and Chancellor, Duke of the State, with hands that turn the wheel of creation, has casually pulled something up from beneath nine fathoms of deep water—a thing that is rugged and coarse. It is not...
"Jiulian! Not a hair's breadth of transgression. He has been placed upon the clouds; all the people of the great earth can only blink their eyes.
Tell me, by what means did he do this? After a long silence, he said: "Zha! (A seal of completion.)

The mountains, rivers, and lakes are laid bare; snow is chiseled and ice carved. Flowers are gathered and brocades clustered. The meaning of neighborliness is ever-shining; the meaning of friendship is ever-bright.
To help a person climb a tree, yet to push them down a well—though the kalpa-stone may be worn away, this resentment shall never perish.
The Dharma seat was no more than a few feet high and no more than a few feet wide. Śāriputra said, "I cannot ascend it;
why do you so willingly humble yourself? Look, look! Today Yangshan takes his place with level steps.
Ascending the seat, he offered incense and made his vows for the Emperor (the question-and-answer portion is not recorded). He then said:

"According to the mandate, at the head of the four rattan canes there is an eye as bright as the sun, specifically inscribed with the *svastika* character. The blue-eyed barbarian monk laughs as it lifts toward the heavens; though its thunder is fierce and its wind swift."
It is already a case of "u-yan" becoming "ma. Therefore it is said: "Speech and activity have no connection;
yet speech and activity also have no connection. As soon as you intend to act thus, it is already not thus. A fresh presentation, held up face-to-face:
within the city of Yuanzhou, the spring terrace stands like a wall, level as a whetstone; beneath Jiyun Peak, the incense burner of the ancient temple.
The mouth faces heaven; a fragrant breeze comes from the south, bringing coolness to the palace halls.

If you can grasp this here and now, you will not have come in vain for more than five hundred li through the summer heat. Thus you may repay the unrequited kindness and assist in the effortless transformation.
If it be otherwise, then a thousand peaks will bow to Mount Hua, and ten thousand streams will flow solemnly into the vast ocean. Again, he cites Luryuan:
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "The essential meaning of that which came from the West is not easy to proclaim. At that time, a monk stepped forward;
Yuan immediately struck him and said, "What kind of occasion is this for you to show your head? He then returned to his quarters. The Master commented:
"A needle in a cloth bag—keeping one's head hidden is the mark of a skilled hand. Layuan was resentful that the monk did not recognize the proper timing.
Let us set that aside for now. Do you know the source of the milk? Let us set aside the fact that the source of the milk does not know; do you, Xinyangshan, know it?
In those days, Bodhidharma had no teeth at all; it was only because he stubbornly forced himself to put his head out.
That evening, there was a small informal sermon (*xiaochan*). Deshan’s small informal sermon was "not answering a word": standing tall atop the highest peak.

Zhaozhou’s small informal sermon, however, was "answering a word": walking deep within the bottom of the sea. Although these two great elders were rivals of equal strength, they could not avoid being like Xu Liu carrying a single board.
One of them, in the hands of Longtan, received a mere scrap of paper and candle, yet he took it to be a full-length staff.
The White Staff: He strikes when the Buddha comes; he strikes when the Patriarch comes. On the borders of Changwu, he sets fires in the high winds and murders under the black moon.
Once, while Nanquan was lying down, he caught several phrases of delirious speech and twisted his tongue around them.
"To those who have already arrived, he says, 'Go drink tea'; to those who have not yet arrived, he also says, 'Go drink tea.

In the distant regions of Youyan, he sells dogs while hanging up sheep, and points to a deer while calling it a horse. Had the two elders known this from the beginning, they would never have committed such acts of expediency to bring harm upon innocent people.
Within the school of the patch-robed monks, there is a single point that even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot master; surely one would not act in such a manner."

"I wish to interrogate him thoroughly and exile him to another region. However, as it is the very beginning of my tenure at this monastery and affairs are currently in a state of great bustle, I shall let him off for now.
Nevertheless, tell me: when Yangshan gives this small evening discourse tonight, is he finally answering the question or not?
After a long silence, he said: "When the power of authority is in one's hand, wait and see when the command is executed. He then cited an ancestor of this mountain.
One day, a strange monk arrived through the air. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The monk replied, "From India. The Master asked, "When did you leave there?
The monk replied, "This morning. The Master said, "Why so late? The monk replied, "I was traveling among the mountains and playing in the waters.

The Master said, "Venerable one, you certainly possess supernatural powers and wondrous functions; however, as for the Buddha-Dharma, it must be returned to this old monk. The monk— [remained silent].

The Master said: "I came to this eastern land to pay homage to Mañjuśrī, yet I encountered a minor Śākyamuni. Thereupon, [Mañjuśrī] produced a *pattraka* leaf and showed it to him, then ascended into the air and departed.
The Master commented: "When a bright mirror stands upon its stand, if a Hu comes, it reflects the Hu; if a Han comes, it reflects the Han."
If that were so, it would indeed be correct. Yet why did this monk smear things over right before his own face? Jiyun had his own authentic command, yet he let him off—what was his intention?
After a long silence, he said: "A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for the sake of a field mouse."
Zhongxia ascends the hall: "In the middle of the sixth month, it is midsummer; everywhere else there is a vacation, but at Dayang it is not so. We hold fast to the end of the rope.
Although the monastery’s resources are nearly non-existent, this cannot trouble our minds; we only worry that you brothers do not understand the saying, 'The dog has no Buddha-nature.
Nevertheless, when the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita sold his heart and liver, who was there before the wind to buy such a chaotic mess?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Upon this lump of red flesh, there is a True Person of No Rank. He enters and exits incessantly through the eyes, the ears, the nose, and the mouth.
Entering and exiting incessantly, he is able to speak and call out; he is able to bend and extend; he is able to like and dislike."
He can rejoice and he can be angry. If you people have not yet had direct evidence of this, then please provide that evidence!
On this day, Jiyun stands as your guarantor. If it is otherwise, what is the "True Person of No Rank"? It is nothing but a dry piece of excrement.
When Master Wushan arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "A precious sword emerges from its scabbard; refined gold leaps from the furnace.

Its luster shines like stars, its brilliance pierces the heavens. Cast into deep waters, its radiance increases all the more; subjected to fierce flames, its color remains without the slightest alteration.
When wielded among men to right injustices, it must surely demand a price as high as the vast heavens."
Ascending the hall: Geese enter the high heavens; crickets chirp upon the ancient steps. We engage in a profound discourse on the Gate of Non-duality and clarify the Single Ultimate Meaning.
Blinding the eyes and stuffing the ears, if you can hear clearly and see intimately, there is no need for a personal transmission of the prediction at the Dragon Flower Assembly.

On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying: "From the Buddhas and patriarchs of the past, their skillful means have been explained in a thousand ways and ten thousand ways, yet they have spoken only of matters on the periphery of light and shadow.
The descendants of later generations, greedily gazing at the heavens above, have missed what is right before their eyes.

Whether striking with a staff or grasping in the water, they become increasingly disconnected from the truth. Now tell me, how can one attain resonance? He then struck the meditation seat with his staff.
[The Master] brandishes the whisk, draws a circle in the air, and says: "On this night, the single orb is full; where is its clear light not present?
On the Double Ninth, he ascends the hall. To discuss the profound and the subtle is like using oil to wash black; to strike with the staff and shout is like gouging out flesh to create a sore.
In various quarters, there is much exaggeration and hyperbole; Jiyun merely deliberates based on what he has personally witnessed and determined.
Why is this? Every year on the ninth day is the Double Ninth Festival.

[He] ascends the hall and says: "The wind moves and the heart sways the tree; clouds arise and nature gives rise to dust. But consider it: when the clouds have not yet arisen and the wind has not yet moved..."
Prior to this, where does the nature of mind reside? Do you all still know? If you can indeed know it, then though whirlwinds topple mountains, they are ever still;
though rivers compete to flow, they do not move; though wild horses gallop and flutter, they do not stir;
though the sun and moon traverse the heavens, they do not complete a circuit. If this is not yet so, you will not realize that day turns to night; how then can one keep people young?
Ascending the hall, he said: "This morning is the twenty-fifth of the twelfth lunar month; tomorrow is the twenty-sixth of the twelfth lunar month.
Before the wind, the song of Yangshan is sung; everyone says it is the melody of Yunmen. This may be so, yet the tonal rhythms differ somewhat.
How can this be seen? After a long silence, he said: 'The lute and the flute are not the same as the human voice.'"
Ascending the hall on New Year’s Day: The first month of the year opens the reign; all things are renewed. If one seeks even a hair’s breadth of the old appearance, it is utterly unobtainable.
Within the peach pit of a thousand years, there is originally but the old kernel. If one seeks even a hair’s breadth of the new appearance, it is utterly unobtainable.

The characteristics of the new and the old cannot be apprehended; that which cannot be apprehended is itself unapprehendable. When the Way prevails and the times are clear, the myriad nations are at peace.
On the first day of the first month of the second year of the Xiachun era.
When the assembly of monks returned from the feast at Mount Wei after entering the city, the Master ascended the hall and addressed the multitude, saying:

"Before the Flying Snow Pavilion and atop the Spring-Enjoyment Terrace, things are ten thousandfold diverse, yet spring remains unchanged. To those who stay and disregard leaving, they still lack a punch to the face;
to those who leave and disregard staying, a slap across the cheek is well-deserved. Even if one forgets both leaving and staying, being like a dragon..."
The elephant has not yet been relieved of his patched robe; [the Master] strikes him repeatedly with a heavy staff. Even when the staff breaks, he does not let go.
Tell me: is this punishment or is it reward? Have you not heard it said: "If one acts for others, one must act thoroughly; if one kills, one must see blood"?

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "On this auspicious occasion of the Upper Yuan Festival at Mount Yangshan, let us set aside the lutes and songs for a moment. The snow has cleared and the mountain colors are as deep as indigo;
the ice has melted and the mountain streams flow over the rocks. There is so much to see that the eyes cannot take it all in; there is so much to hear that the ears cannot comprehend it.
If you all can find your way home here, there will be no need for the further bestowal of the transmission of Dīpaṃkara."

Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "Since the time of the Patriarchs, there has been the discussion of the profound and the marvelous, the fresh picking up and setting down, and the guidance beyond the categories.
All of these are merely circling around the periphery. As for that direct, decisive phrase—how do you speak it? After a long silence, he said:
The spring breeze is piercingly cold; it freezes the young men to death.

The Buddha ascends the hall for the Nirvana discourse. (That night there was thunder and rain. More than two thousand years have passed since the Buddha’s extinction, yet the descendants of those who commit the five heinous crimes have taken no notice at all.
One night, thunder crashed and rain poured down; even the devas could not bear it. You all—
People, do not mistakenly harbor resentment. It was originally this old man who, beneath the twin *śāla* trees, shook the thunder of the Dharma and beat the drum of the Dharma;
he spread the clouds of compassion and sprinkled the nectar of immortality, expounding the single path to *nirvāṇa*.
As for this single path to *nirvāṇa*, when Jiyun makes such a proclamation, is it real or is it false? Have you not heard it said: "I declare that I have entered *parinirvāṇa*"?
"Those who have attained liberation are not my disciples; those who say I have not entered parinirvāṇa are also not my disciples.
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and called to the assembly, saying: "If you have a staff, I shall give you a staff."

"You have no staff; I shall take your staff away! Although this old man Bajiao’s display of giving and taking may be worth observing for a time, he cannot avoid favoring the strong rather than the weak.
Jiyun is not like this: if you have it, he does not give it to you; if you lack it, he does not take it away.
One's own staff is to be carried by oneself. (He strikes once and says: "Application is according to the occasion."
Vibrant and agile, he leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall for the discourse, he said: "Within the domain of each of you, there is a cool, precious palace. Its six gates are wide open and its eight windows are bright and clear.
A fragrant breeze blows constantly; the scorching sun never reaches it. Streams flow upon the roof."
The rain falls through the four seasons; cranes stand upon the tips of pines as the ten thousand realms rest in tranquility. Do you all understand this or not?
If you do understand, each of you may return to your own home and sit in peace. If it is otherwise, then beneath the three rafters and before the seven-foot mat—
Try knocking on the door with a tile.
Upon the lifting of the retreat restrictions, he ascends the hall: "The mouth of the sack is tied shut; the Buddhas of the three periods have no place to draw breath.
When the floodgates are opened, millions of fish and dragons have a path to turn their bodies. They shake their manes and wag their tails, overturning heaven and earth, thundering like a storm."
It seizes lightning and stirs the clouds and mist. Even so, you must still be careful and attentive. But tell me, what is it you are being careful for?
You are being careful lest you be drowned in a jar of fermented soy sauce.

Ascending the hall to thank the two orders of officials, he called to the assembly, saying: "Heaven covers all without partiality by means of the three luminaries; Earth bears all without partiality by means of the five sacred peaks.

To stabilize the state and bring peace to the realm, there are the civil and military officials; to guide disciples and lead the multitude, there are the two classes of attendants from the east and west.
If even one among them falters, then nothing will be accomplished. Holding up his staff, he said: 'As for this very staff, in ordinary times...'"

Supporting heaven and propping up earth; sustaining the precarious and aiding the endangered—does this not still rely on another's power? *He strikes once.* Leaning on his staff and extending his hand, he says:
"Picking it up and putting it down—none of this can do without this very thing."
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the autumn of the eighth month, where is there heat? The fragrance of rice blossoms wafts; the sparse forest sheds its leaves.

Three drops, five drops—rain falling at irregular intervals. One note, two notes—a flute playing from somewhere unknown. If you can, right here, hear that there is nothing to hear, you will realize and enter perfect penetration; this is the foremost."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: My mind is like the autumn moon; the autumn moon is like my mind. Together they illuminate, leaving not a speck of dust;
both are pure, as all sounds sink into silence. So bright and so white, exactly the same in antiquity as it is today.
Were it not for Hanshan, who else could understand this verse?
Ascending the hall: On the ninth month, one is given robes; yet for those who have no robes to receive, there is a distinct essential subtlety within the gate of the patch-robed monks.
How can this be seen? It is not said: "The newly pasted paper quilt is warm when heated; one sleeps through it, wrapped in clothes, until the fifth watch.
Hearing the bells and drums of the upper quarters strike, another day is added to this floating life."

Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "If one can take a single step forward from atop a hundred-foot pole, there will be nothing above to grasp at or look up to, and nothing below to serve as one's own body.
Within the furnace of ten thousand refinements, one is forged until fully perfected—unbreakable when struck and indestructible when hit. Nevertheless..."
Furthermore, you must know that there is a samādhi beyond this. Why? Where the weeds and marshes end, there is the green mountain; the traveler goes even further beyond the green mountain.

On the occasion of the Double Ninth, he ascended the hall: "The autumn rains have just cleared; the autumn sky is as if washed clean. On the ninth day, the chrysanthemums are fresh; the thousand forests are yellow."
The leaves fall. Everyone knows only how to hasten their steps upward; they often miss their own secure and secret ground.
Is there anyone who does not miss it? After a long silence, he said: "Be careful! Be careful!"
Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally non-existent; how could there be a single mind?

Cease all deliberation and forget all conditions, remaining silent and guarding yourself within. If you can do this morning and do this evening, then naturally it will be empty yet spiritual, void yet wondrous.
At this very moment," he then reached out his hand and said, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Jiyun does not understand Zen; he does not understand the Way. He does not recognize the horizontal stroke, nor does he comprehend the vertical stroke.
By day he eats three meals; at night he takes one sleep. As the years pass, old and sick, he becomes increasingly unrefined.
He has not even a skirt or a tunic, yet he possesses the mere semblance of a *kāṣāya*. [The Master] then lifted up his *kāṣāya* and asked: "Do you see it? Do you want it?"
I shall take it away. If this is not yet so, do not take offense at this old monk’s fondness for it.
[The Master] thanks the four head officers for holding the whisk and ascends the hall. He calls to the assembly, saying: "The four-petaled red lotus proclaims its teaching in a single sound."
Its words are skillful and its meaning is profound and far-reaching. It does not deviate by a single point from the majestic sound of the past;
it does not miss by a single point when realized by Maitreya in the future. It transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations; it is neither non-existent nor merely existent.
Just as with one person who is thus, another who is not thus, one who is thus yet not thus, and one who is not thus yet is thus—[it is like this].
"How so? After a long silence, he said: "The craftsmanship differs; they are both rice and flour.
When Chan Master Panlong came to visit, the Master ascended the hall and said: "In the family of patch-robed monks, there is no fixed basis.
Discernment lies before the trigger; subtlety lies in the turning point. He asked: "At Outang, the seat was shared equally; before Jiyun Peak, his solitary style had no peer. Look, look!"
Ninety thousand *zhang* he soars upon the whirlwind; his wings, reaching toward heaven, brush against the clouds and the void.

Entering the city, he returns to the upper hall. On the second day he leaves the city; on the fifth day he returns. At the crossroads, he bumps into Zhang San, who turns out to be the old Li Si from before the mountain.
His features are as they were before, and his speech is as it was of old. He says this again and again: [The original text ends here.]
The Buddha-dharma has declined, and sentient beings are difficult to save. There is no need to force an ox’s head to eat grass, nor is it necessary to join a needle to form an axe.
Why? Because a sweet melon is sweet all the way to its stem, and a bitter gourd is bitter down to its roots.
Ascending the hall on the fifth day of the second month: the myriad flowers vied to burst forth; some displayed their vibrant crimson, others boasted of their refined purity.
Their spirit under the moon, their grace before the wind—how clear and manifest is the ancestral intent, free from any ambiguity! How pitiable and yet how laughable was Old Lingyun.
Mistaking peach blossoms for eyes; even until now, one remains unawakened. Entering the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"A fragrant breeze blows from the south, bringing coolness to the halls and pavilions. Where the Buddhas manifest their bodies, it is brilliantly clear within the mind and eyes.
When the opportunity arises and you face it directly, there is no way to avoid it. I simply wish for you all to open your chests and grasp its meaning."
If this is not yet so, it applies whether you open your eyes or close them.
[The Master] ascends the hall: One month follows another; this month has already passed its fifth day. Why do the two wheels of sun and moon rush so busily?
A hundred years pass in the snap of a finger as if spent in vain. "Things do not shift"—do you know this yet? It is neither Buddha nor Patriarch. Now tell me: [The Master] descends from the seat.
"What, ultimately, is this? After a long silence, he said: "Flowing water does not rot; the pivot of a door does not decay.
To the two classes of officials and those holding the whisk, he ascended the hall and spoke in profound discourse on the Principle: speech is not mere speech; silence is not mere silence.

Appointing to office according to one's capacity—martial is martial, civil is civil. Whether employed or set aside depends on the occasion; the decision lies with me. It is just like taking up a staff...
To take the six-inch golden body and use it as a single blade of grass; to take a single blade of grass and use it as the six-foot golden body—how is this so?
After a long silence, he said: "The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the frontier."
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: My mind is like the autumn moon; yet the Way is something else entirely.
The autumn moon waxes and wanes, but my mind neither diminishes nor increases. Everyone only knows to ascend the tower to admire the view, seeking it in the heavens;
they do not realize that beneath their own robes lies a treasury of radiance—perfectly complete and perfectly pure. Believe this!
Upon seeing through and attaining full penetration, it is not merely a joy for a single night;
it can bring delight for a thousand ages. He ascended the hall and said: "Do not think of good; do not think of evil. Solitary and remote, lively and agile. There is no need to seek it out;
